clue.text: Perhaps Ford's bodyguard is almost stupid about panic

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the shortened word for stupid is read backwards
almost means the word for stupid loses its final letter

parts.note: dumb is a slang word for stupid
a flap is a state of panic or agitation

explanation.surface: A celebrity's minder is mocked as being almost stupid in a moment of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford is the car maker, not a person with a bodyguard: 'almost' trims DUMB to DUM and 'about' turns it to MUD.
explanation.definitionFit: The flap behind a car's wheel guards its bodywork from spray, so a Ford car could have one; an example clue.

clue.text: Auto-test conditions for themes

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
ifs are conditions, as in ifs and buts

explanation.surface: The conditions of a vehicle test serve as themes.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory car safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurring ideas or patterns in a work of art or music are its themes, a synonym.

clue.text: Pad finally getting bye, perhaps on left or on right

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of pad is used

parts.note: in cricket a bye is one kind of extra, a run not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman's pad, a bye, and which side to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Byes are cricket extras: runs taken when the ball passes the batsman without touching bat or pad.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextral describes something on or towards the right-hand side, from Latin dexter.

clue.text: Very big deposit passed round in a negligent way

indicators.note: passed round means the word for deposit goes around the clothing size

parts.note: to lay is to deposit, as a hen lays an egg
XL, extra large, is the clothing size for very big

explanation.surface: A huge deposit was waved through carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something loosely and without care means acting carelessly, a synonym.

clue.text: Scientific historian translated apologies to Zola

indicators.note: translated means the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Apologies offered to the novelist Émile Zola in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges APOLOGIES TO ZOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies fossil animals from ancient eras is in effect a historian of life on earth.

clue.text: Releases universal web addresses hacked by far-right group

indicators.note: hacked by means the far-right group's letters break into the run of letters for universal and web addresses

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
URLs are the addresses of web pages
the NF, the National Front, is a British far-right party

explanation.surface: Websites are attacked by extremist hackers who then publish leaked material.
explanation.walkthrough: The NF is the National Front, a British far-right political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold or open out a flag or sail is to let it loose, a synonym in the verbal sense.

clue.text: In the main, this is not a desirable quality

definitions.text: In the main, this is not a desirable quality

parts.words: In the main, this is not a desirable quality
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a ship unfit to sail on it has an undesirable quality

explanation.surface: A general remark that some quality is mostly unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's unfitness to sail on the ocean is a quality nobody wants on the open sea.

clue.text: At liberty to keep servant on and off till port appears

indicators.note: to keep means the word for at liberty holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: free means at liberty
a man is a manservant

indicators.note: on and off means every other letter of till is taken

explanation.surface: Free to employ a servant now and then until the harbour comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At liberty' reads as describing the servant, but it is the outer word; 'appears' only links. Fremantle is the port of Perth, Western Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the port city serving Perth in Western Australia.

clue.text: Forecast area of pitch before everybody

parts.note: to pitch is to toss or rock, as a ship does at sea
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A weather area for the sports pitch, put ahead of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockall is a sea area in the BBC's Shipping Forecast for British waters, named after a tiny islet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the named sea regions read out in the British Shipping Forecast.

clue.text: Enchanting component of education

definitions.meaning: casting a charm or spell on someone
writing words correctly is one of the basics taught at school

explanation.surface: A charming element of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means casting magic and also the skill of writing words correctly, taught in schools.

clue.text: Stories about topless nooky suppressed by team, duty dodgers?

indicators.note: about means the word for stories goes around everything else

parts.note: tales are stories

indicators.note: suppressed by means the trimmed word sits held down inside the team's letters

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: nooky is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Tabloid tales of a team's sex scandal hushed up, with tax dodging thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressed by team' builds XEXI, the trimmed word held inside the team's eleven; the question mark flags that 'duty' here means tax.
explanation.definitionFit: People who move abroad to avoid paying their home country's taxes are dodging a duty, here a tax rather than an obligation.

clue.text: Compere regularly organised by head of entertainment

definitions.text: Compere regularly organised by head of entertainment

indicators.note: organised means the selected letters are put into a new order
regularly means every other letter of compere is taken, starting with the first
head of means only the opening letter of entertainment is used

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies is routinely booked by the person in charge of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes CMEE from Compere, 'organised' rearranges it to EMCE, and the head of entertainment adds E. The whole clue also describes the answer, a compere hired by an entertainments head.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American term for a master of ceremonies, from the initials MC spelt out, a synonym of compere.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, say, forgets a series of novels

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters of the following words come out in a surprising arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone, say, unexpectedly forgets something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges SAY FORGETS A.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy's linked novels about the Forsyte family form one long saga, an example of a series.

clue.text: Everyone mentioned a boring thing

indicators.note: mentioned means the word for everyone is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody said something was dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed tool for piercing leather or wood bores holes, so it is literally a thing that bores.

clue.text: Intense activity surrounding new kind of pancake

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for intense activity goes around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a blitz is a burst of intense activity

explanation.surface: A frenzy in the kitchen as a new style of pancake is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin rolled pancake with a filling, from Jewish cookery, is one variety of pancake.

clue.text: Fellow's drunk a ninth ale

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are jumbled as if intoxicated

explanation.surface: A man has drunk his ninth beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A NINTH ALE; the 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, such as that of the novelist Hawthorne, stands for a fellow.

clue.text: Door to landing admitting bird

indicators.note: admitting means the phrase lets the answer in, holding it among its letters

explanation.surface: A door opening onto a landing lets a bird in.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European bunting, eaten as a delicacy in France, is a bird.

clue.text: Single drink taken into exam — that's novel

indicators.note: taken into means the letters for single and drink are put inside the word for exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A student sneaks one drink into an exam, a new idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is an adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fresh and never done before is new, a synonym for the adjective.

clue.text: Gentleman put back fragrant oil dish

indicators.note: put back means the word for gentleman is turned round

parts.note: sir is a polite word for a gentleman
otto, also attar, is a fragrant oil from rose petals

explanation.surface: A gentleman returns a fragrant oil in a cooking setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice preparation cooked in stock is a dish.

clue.text: Insulting lingo, mostly imprudent, retracted before opening in speech

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the shortened word is read backwards
mostly means the word for imprudent loses its last letter

parts.note: rash means imprudent

indicators.note: in speech means the word for opening is heard rather than read, giving a spelling that sounds like it

parts.note: a chasm is a deep opening in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone retracts a mostly reckless insult before a speech begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' turns the trimmed RAS round; 'in speech' gives a spelling sounding like chasm, the K sound written as C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting mockery that says the opposite of what it means is a form of insulting language.

clue.text: Quaint, dinky, extremely outdoorsy?

parts.note: twee means quaint, often too sweetly so

indicators.note: extremely means only the two end letters of dinky are taken

explanation.surface: A list of words describing a charming little country cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: tweed is what country types wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dressed in heavy woollen cloth suits the country, hearty, hiking and shooting sort, so being outdoorsy is implied.

clue.text: Setter's redundant digital feature

parts.note: a setter is a gun dog, and many dogs have a useless extra toe higher on the leg

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's unwanted computer function.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter looks like the crossword compiler and digital like computing; it is the dog and its digits, its toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The vestigial claw on the inner side of a dog's foot does no work, so it is a redundant toe.

clue.text: Pair is going north in Great Britain, more or less to climb with equipment

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: the UK is roughly Great Britain, adding Northern Ireland

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Two people head north through Britain on a climbing trip with gear.
explanation.walkthrough: To prusik is to climb a rope using sliding Prusik knots.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means ascending a rope using special friction knots, a technique for climbing with gear.

clue.text: Argue about fish

indicators.note: about means the word for argue is turned round

parts.note: to rag is to scold or rail at someone, a form of arguing

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel over a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin fish with a beak-like snout, also called the needlefish, is a fish.

clue.text: One held in conflict in Crimea to broadcast reactionary aftermath?

indicators.note: to broadcast here means to scatter the letters widely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war, one held captive in a conflict

explanation.surface: A captive in the Crimean conflict is broadcast as a reactionary in the aftermath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to broadcast' rearranges POW, CRIMEA and TO. 'reactionary' is not about politics: it means coming from nuclear reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is what comes after a chain reaction in a reactor, so it is cheekily called what follows a reaction.

clue.text: Previous boss of Monk?

definitions.meaning: the head of a religious house governs its monks; Monk is also this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: Asking who was Monk's former boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Monk is the setter's pseudonym, so the clue teases about the setter's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means earlier, and also the head of a priory, who is a monk's superior.

clue.text: Northern drinkers start to fade by lunchtime in canteen

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a body of former drinkers

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of fade is used

parts.note: one o'clock, written as Roman numeral I, is lunchtime

explanation.surface: Drinkers in the north fade away by lunchtime at a canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) runs canteens and shops for the British armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The British forces' welfare organisation is best known for its canteens, so the name stands for one.

clue.text: Reserve WC, say, where polar explorers may go?

parts.note: to put on ice is to hold in reserve, so ice can mean reserve
W. C. Fields was an American comic actor, an example of someone named Fields

explanation.surface: Booking a lavatory before setting off somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: WC looks like a toilet but is the initials of W. C. Fields, the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flat stretches of permanent ice in the polar regions are the ground that explorers there would cross.

clue.text: How Florence could have been seen by night?

definitions.text: How Florence could have been seen by night?

parts.words: How Florence could have been seen by night?
parts.note: Florence Nightingale was the Lady with the Lamp, seen doing night rounds in the Crimea carrying a light

explanation.surface: A question about how a nurse or a city looked after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence could be the Italian city, but it is Florence Nightingale, the Lady with the Lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by a lamp describes how the nurse carrying one on her rounds would have been seen.

clue.text: Shortly off to stay in an island state

indicators.note: to stay in means the shortened word for off sits inside the island's name

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

indicators.note: shortly means the word for off loses its last letter

parts.note: away means off, as in gone off

explanation.surface: Leaving soon to spend time in an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' cuts AWAY to AWA.
explanation.definitionFit: This region on the island of Borneo is one of the constituent states of Malaysia.
